_meta.description: Oil shipping lanes, chokepoints and pipelines for the globe layer and the simulation engine.
_meta.path_disclaimer: ALL 'path' waypoints are ILLUSTRATIVE geometry hand-placed for drawing on the globe. They are NOT surveyed shipping-lane or pipeline coordinates and are not a sourced data field.
_meta.flow_baseline: Chokepoint flows use EIA calendar-year 2024 (latest full year in EIA's table, last updated 2026-03-03). 2024 Suez/Bab el-Mandeb flows are about half of 2023 because of Red Sea attacks (Suez+SUMED 8.8 -> 4.8 Mb/d; Bab el-Mandeb 9.3 -> 4.1 Mb/d). 1H25 and 2023 values are kept in 'flow_history_mbpd'.
_meta.pipeline_flow_note: For pipelines, 'capacity_bpd' is NAMEPLATE capacity (Global Energy Monitor). Actual throughput is not in our sources, so 'annual_flow_bpd' is null for pipelines. Do not read capacity as flow.

global_reference.source: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints, Table 1 (EIA STEO Feb 2026; Vortexa tanker tracking)

_meta.share_derivation: share_of_global_seaborne_oil_pct = annual_flow_bpd / 79.7 Mb/d (EIA world maritime oil trade, 2024), computed by us from two sourced numbers. Chokepoint shares overlap (a barrel can pass several chokepoints) so they must not be summed.
_meta.importer_note: EIA publishes only group-level destination shares per route, not per-country shares (except China for Malacca and the Cape). Entries marked level='group' are group shares; entries marked derived=true are simple subtractions of sourced numbers. No per-country figure is invented. Shares refer to crude and condensate where stated, not total liquids.

current_conditions.note: Baseline data comes from the last pre-crisis year (2023 or 2024). Real conditions in 2026 differ: EIA reports the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed since early 2026 with production shut-ins across Gulf producers. Treat results as a what-if from a normal baseline, not a forecast of current flows.

current_conditions.source: EIA press release 7 April 2026 and Short-Term Energy Outlook (October 2026), as returned by search; read the linked pages for current figures.

routes.name: Strait of Hormuz

top_importers.country: China, India, Japan and South Korea (combined)
top_importers.basis: share of crude and condensate flows, 2024 (74% in 1H25)

top_exporters.basis: share of crude transiting Hormuz, 2023 (EIA Saudi Arabia Country Analysis Brief, Oct 2024)

routes.bypass_note: EIA's latest combined estimate for Saudi East-West (5.0 Mb/d rated) plus UAE Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline (1.8 Mb/d rated), about 4.7 Mb/d. Older EIA pieces estimated 3.5 Mb/d (with Iran's Goreh-Jask) and 2.6 Mb/d 'effective unused'. Pipelines already carry some oil that never touches Hormuz, so real spare capacity may be lower: treat 2.6 Mb/d as a sensitivity.
routes.baseline_voyage_note: Typical FULL voyage for cargoes using this route (not the transit time through the chokepoint): distance / 14 kn. Estimate: distance is from illustrative waypoints.
routes.source: EIA, World Oil Transit Chokepoints; EIA Today in Energy 2025-06 'Amid regional conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains critical oil chokepoint' and 2023 'The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most important oil transit chokepoint'
routes.baseline_year_note: Last full pre-disruption year in EIA's table (first-half 2025 figures are also stored).

routes.bypass_note: See capacity_resolution. Owner list is partial.

capacity_resolution.finding: Second GEM record (P2044, 321,315 bpd) is a separate capacity INCREMENT, not a double-count.
capacity_resolution.arithmetic: At about 7.33 bbl per tonne: 1,340,000 bpd = 67 Mt/yr; 321,315 bpd = 16 Mt/yr; 67 + 16 = 83 Mt/yr.
capacity_resolution.corroboration: Interfax (2023) reports CPC debottlenecking to 83 Mt/yr; 2018 expansion reached 67 Mt/yr. EIA still cites about 1.4 Mb/d.
capacity_resolution.decision: capacity_bpd stays at the 1.34 Mb/d EIA-consistent figure (conservative). capacity_upper_bpd = 1.66 Mb/d is the case if the debottlenecking is fully realised. Sources are secondary, so this stays an estimate.
